worst: Six medium-severity, adversarially-confirmed defects sit directly in the app's core value proposition — "shows what a shift is worth before it's worked" — and at least three of them make the *preview* price wrong in ordinary, easy-to-hit scenarios rather than edge cases: wage-math-12 (Add-Shift sheet defaults to 'night' and prices it even when the Night differential is switched off), wage-math-10 (pattern-lab template/fixed brush cells silently skip the weekend-differential inference the grid hint promises them, so two identical-looking Saturday cells price $78 apart), and wage-math-01 (a blanked or garbage differential multiplier silently coerces to 0×, pricing every shift of that type at $0 with no warning). Layered on top: wage-math-00 (the hero's 'Taxes & deductions' chip can show a bigger number than gross and disagree with the Breakdown a tap away), wage-math-06 (paystub import can turn a premium-only earnings row into a negative differential), and wage-math-09 ('take-home per paycheck' is presented as a fact when it's a multi-paycheck average for any cycle that doesn't divide 14, with no on-screen qualifier). None of these were rejected or left unverified — all six are confirmed as they stand today.
toReachEight: Fix all six confirmed medium findings, prioritizing the three that corrupt a live preview price rather than just a summary label: (1) gate hourlyRate/shiftGross/patternCellShiftType/brushCell everywhere on the differential's `active` flag, not just in Settings' chip filter, so a disabled or deleted differential is never silently priced (closes wage-math-01, wage-math-10, wage-math-12 together — they're the same root cause in three call sites); (2) cap the hero 'Taxes & deductions' chip the same way computeNet caps pre/post for display, or reconcile the two so they can never disagree (wage-math-00); (3) make paystub-import classification treat a premium-only row as a positive differential rather than flipping its sign (wage-math-06); (4) add an explicit 'average — your actual paycheck will vary' qualifier wherever patternMetrics' per-paycheck figure is shown for a cycle that doesn't divide 14 (wage-math-09). Given this is a paycheck-math app, also clear the nine low-severity findings (independently-rounded chips, Infinity%-on-zero-goal, float-precision hours display, weekend-pickup card pricing a disabled differential, sampleNet's hand-rolled tax formula) before calling the surface clean — they're low severity individually but there are nine of them clustered in the same money-display code.

No slice covered `te_swap_p2_algo.js` or `rls_audit.js` (both absent from git, per CLAUDE.md) — those figures remain unreproduced by this run.
worst: security-00 [critical, confirmed, live-verified on the production project]: poster_key — the entire anonymity mechanism of the swap board — is reversible. The 'scrubpay-swaps' salt is a public constant (the repo is public), and the "see co-members" policy plus full-table grants on swap_members/swap_groups let any member read the underlying user_ids, including the board creator's. This doesn't just weaken the anonymity model docs/swap-board.md claims was audited 29/29+5/5 — it defeats it outright for every live unit group, meaning a real nurse's identity is recoverable by any colleague in her group before any match is confirmed. Combined with security-01 (propose_swap has no check that the caller is actually a party to the swap, so any member can silently reserve and hide two other people's posts) and security-02 (a raw UPDATE policy bypasses decline_swap_match and can permanently strand a post as 'proposed'), the swap board's core trust properties are broken in production, not just theoretical.
toReachEight: Fix the critical anonymity break first: derive poster_key from a private per-deployment secret (not a public repo constant) and tighten swap_members/swap_groups grants/policies so members can only see what the anonymity model intends (posted-count, not user_id) — this alone is necessary but likely not sufficient given how many co-dependent RPCs assume the current shape. Then close the two high findings: add a leg-membership check to propose_swap, and put a real server-side byte-size CHECK/trigger on user_data.data (client-side MAX_BLOB_BYTES is not a bound). Then work through the six confirmed mediums: route the decline UPDATE path through decline_swap_match only, validate shift_meta before writing it into another member's shifts in doApplyPlan, require ical-proxy to authenticate the actual signed-in user (not just possession of the public anon key), clear icalSub/icalUrl/hydratedUserId on sign-out and resetToDefaults, switch Google sign-in to the PKCE flow, and cap/validate the client_error batch against the live events_props_check constraint before flushing so it can't be silently dropped. Until the critical finding is fixed, no amount of progress on the others reaches 8 — a broken anonymity guarantee on a feature whose entire pitch is anonymity is disqualifying on its own.

Per ranAgainst.json the reviewers read sanitizeData, hourlyRate/shiftGross/computeNet/patternMetrics, saveToSupabase/loadCloudRow, writeBackup/readBackup, serializeState/applyData/hydrateFromCloud, the auth session + SIGNED_IN/SIGNED_OUT handling, the debounced-save effect and its MAX_BLOB_BYTES guard, the pagehide/visibilitychange flush, retrySync, the 15s cross-device poll with its content-equality normalize(), saveDayShifts, the full ICS parse/plan/confirm/re-sync pipeline plus ical-proxy's SSRF guard, and migrations 000/002/003 (confirmed no CAS/trigger on user_data). worst: data-integrity-00 (high, confirmed): the pagehide/visibilitychange flush handler (index.html:2489-2505) calls saveToSupabase(...).then(ts=>{ if(ts){...} }) with no else branch -- verified live at index.html:2496. The debounced save effect 20 lines above it (2470-2479) explicitly handles this exact failure mode with writeBackup() on a falsy result; flush was never given the same guard. Concretely: a signed-in nurse edits a shift and immediately backgrounds or closes the tab within the 500ms debounce window (exactly the case this handler exists for) on a flaky connection -- the best-effort save fails, nothing is written to BACKUP_KEY, and once the tab is gone the edit is unrecoverable on next load: no toast, no syncError, no backup, unlike every other save-failure path in the app. This is a genuine, narrow-but-real silent data-loss bug, not a restatement of the documented last-writer-wins tradeoff.
toReachEight: Fix data-integrity-00: give flush the same writeBackup-on-failure branch the debounced effect has (ideally write the backup synchronously before the best-effort save fires, since a .then() continuation isn't guaranteed to run once teardown starts) and negative-test it in the harness (kill the network mid-flush, assert the backup key holds the edit). That single fix clears the only confirmed finding this run; the other 6 raised in this lens were rejected as restating the already-documented last-writer-wins/no-CAS design rather than surfacing new defects, so nothing else here is owed. Score would land at or above 8 once this one fix ships and is verified against a real teardown, not just a passing debounce.

ranAgainst: All 10 code-quality slices in docs/council-runs/2026-09-13/ranAgainst.json (code-quality:boot, wage-core, money-surfaces, calendar, add-shift, pattern-lab, onboarding, settings-etc, swap-board, data-sync, calendar-sync, telemetry-auth, infra -- 13 slice-entries covering the full ~5,800-line index.html plus all 4 SQL migrations, both GitHub workflows, check_build.mjs, and tests/harness.mjs+smoke.mjs). Findings inventory: 17 confirmed (4 high: 00,01,11,18; 13 medium: 02,03,04,05,07,09,13,14,19,22,24,25,29), 6 rejected (06,17,20,23,27,28, do not count), 8 low-severity unverified (08,10,12,15,16,21,26,30, weighed lightly).
worst: A recurring root-cause pattern, not a single bug: near-identical logic is written twice (or three times) at sibling call sites, and the copies drift. code-quality-00 (high) -- handleSignOut doesn't mirror the SIGNED_OUT onAuthStateChange cleanup it's modeled on, so the previous user's iCal credential survives into the next sign-in on a shared device. The same shape recurs in code-quality-11 (high, sign-out resets onboarding data but not obStep, letting a stale wizard silently commit defaulted data), code-quality-19 (medium, MAX_BLOB_BYTES is checked at only 1 of 3 save call sites -- the debounced save has it, flush() and retrySync() don't), code-quality-18 (high, the pagehide/visibility flush silently drops a failed save with no backup, unlike the debounced-save path a few lines up), code-quality-14 (medium, the body-scroll-lock effect's dependency list omits showShare), and the low-severity cluster (08/10/21: the hours-clamp literal, the ISO-validity check, and post-save bookkeeping are each copy-pasted 3x). None of these are one-off typos -- each is a case where the file already had the correct behavior somewhere else in the same component family and a sibling branch just didn't get it, which is exactly what "single 5,800-line file, two god components, no shared helpers" predicts.
toReachEight: Extract the duplicated branches into single shared functions so a fix lands everywhere at once: one sign-out/reset routine that both handleSignOut and the SIGNED_OUT auth listener call (closes 00 and 11); a shared saveWithGuards() that flush(), retrySync() and the debounced save all funnel through so the MAX_BLOB_BYTES check and the failed-save backup apply uniformly (closes 18, 19); fix the body-scroll-lock effect's dependency array (14); replace runIcalSync's bare swallow-everything catch with the same console.error mirror used elsewhere (22); add an explicit allowlist for ficaWithholdingType in sanitizeData, matching the estimateMode whitelist pattern already used two lines away (01); and de-duplicate the hours-clamp/ISO-validity/day-key literals into one helper each. That's roughly 6-8 targeted edits addressing a shared root cause, not 17 independent fixes -- but until they land, the app has multiple confirmed silent-data-loss and silent-credential-leak paths, which keeps this lens well under the bar.

toReachEight: Fix the five confirmed high-severity findings, all of which puncture the "no surprises" promise in ordinary, non-edge usage: (00) hero's "Taxes & deductions" chip vs. the Breakdown a tap away disagreeing whenever flat deductions exceed a $0-gross period -- the default state at the start of every pay period; (04) Pattern Lab's "Take-home per paycheck" shown with zero hedge for cycles like the shipped 4-on/4-off preset, where real paychecks swing ~$1,800 above/below the displayed average; (05) the welcome screen's hardcoded sample figure disagreeing with the app's own sampleNet() math for the identical schedule -- the app contradicts itself inside one onboarding session; (06) "Clear the sample" leaving the fictitious $65.15/hr rate in place with no signal it isn't real once the honesty banner is gone, so every subsequent figure is silently wrong; (08) wiring baseRate/keepRatio into SwapsSheet so a nurse sees an estimated take-home or $/hr before Propose, not after commit.
